The fix is committed (f2eabee9 on b2e0a5c8) and bundled. It roughly halves 58's cost rows, but 11 rows are still over tolerance, so under your standing rule I'm naming that cost rather than calling the bundle clean.

<to_controller>
/work/fix58-ctxcost.bundle (b2e0a5c8..f2eabee9): one commit, one file (item_context_reads.av), verified.
Cost slice, same machine, store off:
- b2e0a5c8 as is: `cost: 54 rows, 21 over, 32 fell`
- with f2eabee9: `cost: 54 rows, 11 over, 42 fell`
What the commit does:
- Three cut queries, `package_contexts`, `library_contexts` and `closure_contexts`. All three read `file_contexts` and never re-derive it.
- A file's import closure is built only where its program can declare a context. Library files are gated on what their package's library declares, so the compiler's ctx test programs no longer make every std-avrac file build its closure.
- check-cli and cold-with-store-fill are back inside tolerance.
The 11 rows still over are not mine, so this cost is named, not fixed:
- Rows: build-cli +4.1% boxes and +6.3% retains; check-program +1.4% retains.
- Sites (census, base57 vs this tree): item_context.av `held_part` +12.5M, engine `part_of_answer_held` +10.3M, `hash.held` +8.7M, `octets_at` +7.1M, `declaration_of` +3.4M. They come from 029a2829 (items), dc712bb2 (engine) and 5d43adf9 (signatures). Nothing of mine is left in the build-cli diff.
Laws hold on a built w58f: all ten ctx refusal cases (durable_db_unset too), ctx suite 6/6, queue_store idioms 0 refusals, decl_grain 13/13, `check packages/std-avrac` 161 s.
Next: I'll port the fix to my lane, where the base is my own (no 72629be7).
</to_controller>

    ctx: the read survey is scoped to the program a file stands in, and meets each body once
    
    Building or checking a program in std-avrac spun without end (batch 58's timeouts):
    contained_task and cleanup_unwinding_trap never finished `run`, nor did `check packages/std-avrac`.
    The laws that read the survey — `ctx.required` (every entry judged, 03a7aab3), `ctx.cached` and the
    unread set — took the contexts a package's files declare, so one test program of std-avrac
    declaring a required context had every item of the package walk a survey: for `ctx.cached`, of
    every entry of the whole package, afresh for each `@query` item. Each visit then scanned the
    survey's met calls, open bodies and fn values as lists of names, so a round was quadratic in the
    bodies it met.
    
    Each law now reads the contexts the file's own closure declares (`entry_contexts`): a context a
    body reads is declared in a file its file reaches. A file that runs is a program of its own, so its
    survey walks its own entry only; any other is surveyed over its package's programs, as before.
    The survey's seen sets are maps: a body is met, opened and taken as a value once a round, and its
    rounds stay the fixed point they were, bounded by ROUNDS. The package-wide `contexts_declared`
    query, which nothing reads now, goes.
    
    features/ctxs/tests/value_cycle holds the loop's shape: fn values that call each other through
    values, under `contained` and a `defer`, reading a context set above them — eval == native ==
    expected.

    declaring a required context had every item of the package walk a survey: for `ctx.cached`, of
    every entry of the whole package, afresh for each `@query` item. Each visit then scanned the
    survey's met calls, open bodies and fn values as lists of names, so a round was quadratic in the
    bodies it met.
    
    Each law now reads the contexts the file's own closure declares (`entry_contexts`): a context a
    body reads is declared in a file its file reaches. A file that runs is a program of its own, so its
    survey walks its own entry only; any other is surveyed over its package's programs, as before.
    The survey's seen sets are maps: a body is met, opened and taken as a value once a round, and its
    rounds stay the fixed point they were, bounded by ROUNDS. The package-wide `contexts_declared`
    query, which nothing reads now, goes.
    
    features/ctxs/tests/value_cycle holds the loop's shape: fn values that call each other through
    values, under `contained` and a `defer`, reading a context set above them — eval == native ==
    expected.

src=$out/src
mkdir -p "$src/build"
git archive "$snapshot" | tar -x -C "$src"
cp "$compiler" "$src/build/avra"
find build -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -name '*.o' -o -name '*.a' -o -name '*.so' -o -name 'avra_hot.bc' -o -name 'avra_hot.inc' \) \
    -exec cp {} "$src/build/" \;
printf '%s\n' "$snapshot" > "$out/snapshot"
cache=$root/$out/cache

# One run of the census compiler in the snapshot, once what it reads is older than the stamp window:
# its census to <name>.out, what it printed to <name>.stdout. The machine's store is off unless the
# workload's `store` is `filled`: then on, in the run's own cache, which every cold run starts bare.
counted() {
    name=$1; shift
    machine=0
    [ "${store:-off}" != filled ] || machine=1
    sleep 3
    started=$(date +%s)
    # the census reports at exit only where the run accounts (AVRA_MEM_STATS)
    (cd "$src" && unset AVRA_MACHINE_STORE_DIR && AVRA_MACHINE_STORE=$machine AVRA_MEM_STATS=1 AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$cache" AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1 \
        sh "$root/tools/memcap.sh" "${COST_CAP_MB:-8000}" taskset -c 0 build/avra "$@" \
        > "$root/$out/$name.stdout" 2> "$root/$out/$name.out") || {
        tail -20 "$out/$name.out"; echo "cost: $name failed ($*)"; exit 1; }
    echo "cost: $name $(($(date +%s) - started)) s"
}

warm() {
    counted "$1" tapes --findings packages/cli

#!/bin/sh
# THE EXACT-COUNT GATE'S MEASUREMENT: the census compiler of this tree, run over FIXED workloads whose
# sources are one pinned commit (the `snapshot` row of tools/cost.baseline): cold, each run's census
# kept as build/cost/<workload>.out; and warm after each edit of a fixed set, the answers it worked out
# again kept as build/cost/edit-<kind>.out. tools/cost_ratchet.py judges them.
#   sh tools/cost.sh                      the baseline's snapshot
#   COST_SNAPSHOT=<sha> sh tools/cost.sh  another snapshot (what `make cost-accept` records)
#   COST_COMPILER=<file> sh tools/cost.sh a census compiler already built from this tree
#
# A FIXED INPUT MEASURES THE COMPILER: the snapshot is exported whole, std included, and the census
# compiler stands at its build/avra beside the objects a build links, so every package it reads is
# the snapshot's.
# ONE PROCESS ON ONE CORE DOES ALL THE WORK: a forked worker's counts are its own, so no body is
# lowered ahead (AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF) and the run is held to one core (`taskset`), the width every
# emitter reads, so objects are made in this process by one worker.
# EVERY COLD RUN STARTS BARE: an empty store, and no product a run before it left, which a build reads.
# A FILE IS READ ONLY ONCE IT IS OLDER THAN THE STAMP WINDOW (io.stamp withholds a stamp from a path
# changed in the last two seconds), so what a run stamps never depends on how fast it began.
snapshot=${COST_SNAPSHOT:-$(awk '$1 == "snapshot" { print $2 }' tools/cost.baseline 2> /dev/null)}
[ -n "$snapshot" ] || { echo "cost: tools/cost.baseline names no snapshot"; exit 1; }
# A SHALLOW CLONE FETCHES THE ONE COMMIT IT PINS.
# The cold workloads: a name, the machine's store it runs over, then the command the census compiler
# runs in the snapshot. A STORE IS NOT THE COMPILER: every run but one has the machine's store off, so
# its rows are what the compiler does, whatever a store holds; `cold-with-store-fill` is the cli's
# cold check over an empty store, which it fills — the store's own price, ratcheted apart.

mkdir -p /tmp/claude-0/s7 && cat > /tmp/claude-0/s7/commit.txt <<'EOF'
std-ui: the theme is a context — `ctx theme`, set once at the board's page, stamped where it differs

std-ui declares `ctx theme: Theme = plain()`. Nothing takes a theme by argument any more: `app`,
`mount`, `paged`, `render`, `hydration` and the live page's `paint*` lose their theme parameter, and
`Env` its theme field. A node carries the theme it was drawn in as a `Stamp` where its frame's entry
for `ctx theme` differs from the nearest one drawn above it — one pointer compare per primitive
(`@std.meta.ctx_entry`, lowered to the new `avra_ctx_entry` row), one stamp per set. The root is
always stamped.

Every realizer honors a nested stamp. Headless and the terminal carry the nearest stamp down and
answer `theme_of(words)`. The DOM and HTML draw the root's theme as the page's, and a nested one
under a class its theme names (`th-…`): its variables set on that element, which the cascade nests,
and its look under the chain of scopes it stands in, so the nearest scope is always the most
specific.

The board's `theme()` goes. `board_page` sets `ctx theme` once from `dark`, with Crisp as data.
tools/ui-board/flip flips `dark` by its control under AVRA_EXACT=check: every turn is held to the
full paint (answered 0, declined 4). realize/tests/nested_theme_test holds a subtree in another
theme, and one back in the page's inside it, on all four realizers.
EOF
echo ok

381-/// THE DOOR LAW, AND THE ONE PLACE A PATH IS CHOSEN: every command that reads a program — `build`,
382-/// `run`, `check`, `test` — takes the program layer, for a package's directory and for a lone file
383-/// alike, or refuses once, naming what the layer cannot do yet; it never takes the old path instead.
384:/// `AVRA_PROGRAM=0` alone takes the old path.
385-// LICENSED input.debug_flag: which path answers during the switch, never an input of an answer
386:export fn program_door() -> bool { env("AVRA_PROGRAM") != "0" }
387-
388-/// THE NET, chosen beside the path: on the program layer the old path judges each program first — a
389-/// build what its own build reads, a check what its own check reads (`NetJudge`) — and what it
390-/// refuses stops there in its words; the program layer builds only what it
391:/// accepts, so a refusal the layer says after it is the layer's defect. `AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0` takes
392-/// the net away.
393-// LICENSED input.debug_flag: which path answers during the switch, never an input of an answer
394:export fn program_net() -> bool { program_door() && env("AVRA_PROGRAM_NET") != "0" }
395-
396-/// What the old path judges a program by, as the old path's own command for it reads it: a build or a run,
397-/// the entry's reach, analysed, before anything is lowered; a check, the whole package as its entry
398-/// sees it; a test, the whole package the path stands in, which its suite reads with no entry of its
399-/// own.
400-export enum NetJudge {
401-    Build
402-    Check
403-    Proved
404-}
405-
406-/// What the net said of a program before the program layer reads it: nothing, where the net is off;
407-/// the old path's acceptance; or its refusal, in its words.
408-export enum NetSaid {
409-    Off
410-    Accepted
411-    Refused(report: string)
412-}
413-
414-/// The net over `paths`: the old path's judgement of each, as `judge` names it.
415-export fn net_said(paths: List<string>, judge: NetJudge) -> NetSaid {
416-    if !program_net() { return NetSaid.Off }
417-    let report? = paths.find_map((p) -> net_report(p, judge)) else { return NetSaid.Accepted }
418-    NetSaid.Refused(report)
419-}

#!/bin/sh
# THE GATE, IN SLICES: every receipt a landing is held to, cut into slices that each run alone in a
# tree of their own, so N machines run N slices at once and the gate takes as long as its longest
# slice. A slice builds the compiler of HEAD itself when build/avra was built from anything else,
# runs every row on the program layer, the net off but where a row's claim is the net, empties the
# stores a cold row reads, bounds every command, keeps each row's words under build/gate/<slice>/, and
# ends with ONE line:
#   GATE <slice> <sha8> PASS|FAIL rows=<n> failed=<n> <seconds>s
# exiting 0 on PASS, 1 on FAIL.
#
#   sh tools/gate.sh list               each slice, one a line, with what it holds
#   sh tools/gate.sh <slice> [arg]      one slice; the idioms slices take the base sha their diff starts at
#   sh tools/gate.sh seed               build/gate/compiler-<sha8>.tar.gz: HEAD's compiler — ONE generation, built
#                                       here first where none of HEAD's stands — and every object a tree
#                                       links with; `pack` is its other name. Run it once; every slice
#                                       then starts from `unpack` and builds nothing.
#   sh tools/gate.sh unpack <file>      seeds this tree from a pack, and holds its stamp to HEAD's: a
#                                       seeded slice builds no compiler
#
7:    pack=$(cd "$(dirname "$1")" && pwd)/$(basename "$1")
8:    refused() { echo "gate: $(basename "$pack") $1 — not seeded" >&2; exit 1; }
28:    echo "gate: seeded from $(basename "$pack") — build/avra stands as HEAD's compiler"

    cat <<'EOF'

#!/bin/sh
# The exact path's own tests, run natively under AVRA_EXACT=check: each program
# in std-ui's realize/dom/tests, and the board's programs under tools/ui-board,
# that has a `.check` file must print exactly
# that, which names how many turns the exact path answered and how many it
# declined. With the flag unset the same programs print their `.expected`
# (the path is off), so eval == native == expected holds for the suite as it is.
# usage: sh tools/exact-patches/check_tests.sh [avra-binary]
set -eu
# usage: paint_measure.sh <label> — builds the paint program with /work/avra's compiler, census and shipping, and times it
. /etc/profile.d/avra.sh; export AVRA_MEM_POOL_MB=12500
L=$1; P=/tmp/claude-0/s7/paint; O=/tmp/claude-0/s7/paint-$L.sum; : > $O
cd /work/avra
counted="-DAVRA_CENSUS -fno-omit-frame-pointer"
make --no-print-directory CFLAGS_avra_runtime="$counted" CFLAGS_avra_hot="$counted" build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null 2>&1
AVRA_FRAME_POINTERS=1 AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES=1 AVRA_INLINE_RUNTIME=0 AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release timeout 900 build/avra-try build $P > /tmp/claude-0/s7/b-$L.log 2>&1; echo "census build $?" >> $O
cp $P/src/main /tmp/claude-0/s7/paint-census-$L
AVRA_MEM_STATS=1 /tmp/claude-0/s7/paint-census-$L > /tmp/claude-0/s7/c-$L.out 2>&1
grep -E "^first|^rc:|^alloc: [0-9]" /tmp/claude-0/s7/c-$L.out >> $O
make --no-print-directory build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null 2>&1
AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release timeout 900 build/avra-try build $P > /dev/null 2>&1
cp $P/src/main /tmp/claude-0/s7/paint-ship-$L
best=999999999; for r in $(seq 1 15); do s=$(date +%s%N); /tmp/claude-0/s7/paint-ship-$L > /dev/null; e=$(date +%s%N); t=$(( (e-s)/1000 )); [ $t -lt $best ] && best=$t; done
echo "best of 15: $best us" >> $O
echo DONE >> $O

// proves: the board is a REAL screen — tasks with done-state, three filters,
// adding from a field, a derived count and progress, a card/row/column/item
// layout and a dialog — and the screen is a function of module `state`. The
// controls are the library's OWN (`button`, `checkbox`, `field`) with
// `on <kind> { … }` handlers, and the task rows are one KEYED list. The test
// speaks to the screen as a reader would — to a control by its words — and
// the loop paints after every event that ran a handler.
use @std.ui.components.{
    button,
    card,
    checkbox,
    column,

use @std.ui.style.style.{Style}

/// Which tasks the board shows.
enum Show { All, Active, Done }

type Todo = { id: string, title: string, done: bool }

state filter: Show = .All
state dark: bool = false
state dialog_open: bool = false
state draft: string = ""
state seq: int = 5
state tasks: List<Todo> = [
    Todo { id: "t1", title: "Draft the spec", done: true },
    Todo { id: "t2", title: "Wire the event channel", done: false },
    Todo { id: "t3", title: "Land the wasm board", done: false },
    Todo { id: "t4", title: "Write the tour", done: true },
]

fn done_count() -> int { [t for t in tasks if t.done].length }

fn admits(t: Todo) -> bool {
    match filter { .All -> true, .Active -> !t.done, .Done -> t.done }
}

fn visible() -> List<Todo> { [t for t in tasks if admits(t)] }

fn theme_label() -> string { if dark { "Light mode" } else { "Dark mode" } }

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - The Avra self-hosting compiler. `make try` builds build/avra-try; gen-2 means rebuilding with that product.
   - rt rows live in core/runtime_api.av, with `RtHost` variants in core/ir.av. Generated files are `./avra runtime-header > runtime/avra_rt.h` and `./avra runtime-namespace > packages/std-avrac/src/features/rt.av`. The keepers are `make rt-header rt-ns`.
   - `make parser` regenerates and differentials the untold parser.
   - DIAGNOSTICS.md and VOICES.md are regenerated by `avra diagnostics` and `avra voices --report`. The voices gate is `voices --baseline tools/voices.baseline`.

   - The idiom gate runs old path: `AVRA_PROGRAM=0 AVRA_MEM_CEILING_MB=12000 check packages/cli --baseline tools/idioms.baseline`, which covers std-avrac sources.
   - Census of a program:
     - Build the runtime with `make CFLAGS_avra_runtime="-DAVRA_CENSUS -fno-omit-frame-pointer" CFLAGS_avra_hot=… build/libavra_runtime.a`.
     - Build the program with `AVRA_FRAME_POINTERS=1 AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES=1 AVRA_INLINE_RUNTIME=0 AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release build/avra-try build <pkg>`.
     - Run it with AVRA_MEM_STATS=1, then restore the shipping lib with `make build/libavra_runtime.a`.
   - ctx frames:
     - `avra_ctx_read(key)` returns a cell or NULL.
     - `@std.meta.ctx_entry(ctx.x)` is a direct call lowered to the new row `avra_ctx_entry(key)`, answering the cell word or 0.
   - Placed frames (A2) make a composition's `ctx` set reach the describe of the children it places.
   - std-ui: `@derive(View)` primitives are generated in tree/view.av; compositions are drawn through `made_of`. `Standing.children` propagates to child standings.
   - The DOM realizer is realize/dom/live.av, and html is realize/html/{html,css}.av. Tokens are CSS custom properties (`var(--tone-…)`); `root_vars`, `look_sheet` and `page_sheet` build the sheet. `AVRA_EXACT=check` runs the exact path beside the full paint and traps on disagreement. Programs with `.check` files run via tools/exact-patches/check_tests.sh (`make exact-patches`).
   - The sandbox can't link wasm (no -lsetjmp), so tools/ui_board.sh's 78 claims can't run here; they need the lead's Mac.

3. Files and Code Sections (step 5, all UNCOMMITTED in /work/avra on branch avra-lane-ui-language-item2; the lane head is 1e2c739b, which includes ctx.cached):
   - packages/std-meta/src/meta.av: added
     ```
     export fn ctx_entry<T>(_read: T) -> int { 0 }
     ```
     with a doc comment: the compiler lowers a DIRECT CALL whose argument is a `ctx.name` read.

   - core/runtime_api.av has the row `avra_ctx_entry` (I64 → I64, host CtxEntry, Reach.Pure, inert), and core/ir.av has the `CtxEntry` RtHost.
   - interp.av dispatches `.CtxEntry -> self.ctx_entry_val(vals)`. interp_tasks.av has:
     ```
     fn ctx_entry_val(vals) -> Val { let id? = array_id(self.frame_cell(self.whole(vals[0]))) else { return Val.I(0) }; Val.I(id + 1) }
     ```
   - runtime/avra_runtime.c has `int64_t avra_ctx_entry(int64_t key)`, which scans the frame and returns the cell word or 0, with its prototype in avra_runtime.h.

content.text:
The rulings, in short:
- **Theme stamp:** stamp a node where the theme differs from its parent's, and honor the stamp on every realizer.
- **The compare:** test the frame's entry by identity, one pointer compare per primitive. Read the value only where a stamp is due.
- **The DOM:** honor a stamp with CSS custom properties, or refuse it aloud.
- **The lazy-reads receipt** rides step 5; the lint comes after the board bundles.

First, the identity compare. Avra code can't name a context's key. But A2 gave `@std/meta` a `Frame` door for placed views, so I'll see what it offers:

message.content:
Lead: the UI lead's rulings on step 5.
1. THEME STAMP: stamp where it differs, AND honor it. A nested theme is never silently drawn in the root's.
- Compare the frame's theme ENTRY by identity, not the theme by value: one pointer compare per primitive, one stamp per `ctx theme = …` set. The root always carries it.
- "Realizers read only the root's" is not accepted: a stamped subtree drawn in the root's theme is the same silent wrong answer.
- Headless and terminal: honor it now. The realizer's walk carries the nearest stamp down, as one variable.
- DOM: if tokens reach the page as CSS custom properties, honor it by setting them on the stamped element (the cascade nests). If they're resolved to literal values, say so with the cost; until it's built, a non-root stamp the DOM can't honor is a SPOKEN refusal at realize, never a quiet draw.
- Test: a subtree set to another theme inside the board's, each realizer drawing it right or refusing by name.
- Report boxes and ms against 11,756 / 1,993 / 3.0 ms.
2. OWED PROGRAMS:
- Lazy ctx_reads: write it as an incremental receipt (a deep edit that leaves a fn's read set alone recomputes no caller). It rides step 5 if small.
- The lint: its rule is already in your design 4 and runs the OTHER way: "a ctx read only by fns whose every caller sets it on the line before the call is a warning: a parameter would do" (the width/wrap example). No "a parameter should be a ctx" lint. Build it AFTER the board bundles, with its true-positive rate measured over the tree first (expect 0 sites; the example is the witness).

content.text:
The step 3b design (placed frames) already makes a set in the root composition reach every descendant's `describe`. What it doesn't settle is the realizer. Today it gets the theme by argument (`live.patches(root, theme)`, the stylesheet, `hydration`) and runs in the app's paint, outside the board's set. So, with no argument threading, the theme has to ride the drawn tree. That choice shapes every realizer, so it goes to the lead before I build it.

<to_controller>
step 5 started. One design point needs the UI lead before I touch realizers:
- What I'm building: std-ui gets `ctx theme: Theme = plain()`. App, mount and paged lose their `theme` seats. Realizers take no theme argument.
- The problem: the board sets `ctx theme` in its root composition, but realizers run in the app's paint, outside that set. Node styles are tokens (`.Surface`, …) that the realizer resolves through a theme, so the theme in force where nodes are drawn has to reach the realizer through the tree.
- Proposal: a primitive's `describe` stamps the theme in force onto its Node only where it differs from the theme its parent was drawn under, and the root always carries it. The cost is one ctx read and one compare per primitive, and a stamp only where a set changes it. Realizers read the root's theme for the page sheet, as today with one theme per page; a nested themed subtree (scoped classes) is left for later.

- **A theme is a typed record.** A misspelled role is a compile error, where a text-keyed map
  answers an empty value.
- **A role's value may be "what the system uses"**, which is how the default theme is native.
- **Colour roles come as a background and what sits on it**, so every pair's contrast is proved at
  build time, in every mode (against WCAG 2.x).
- **Light and dark, contrast and text size are dials the OS turns**, not separate themes.
- **About fourteen colour roles**: canvas, surface at three levels, accent, neutral, danger,
  success, warning, text, muted, disabled, border, focus, link.
- **A state's look (hover, pressed, disabled) is derived from its role**, so one brand colour moves
  every state; on a native control the state is the OS's.
- **A theme reaches a subtree through `ctx theme`.**

# ctx step 3, part b: the walk ("placed, not written"), a ruling ask

## The fact
std-ui's generated composition does this:

    fn made() -> List<dyn View> { let made = gathered { <body> }; made.items }
    fn describe(at) { made_of(at, me.made(), self.key) }

The body's `ctx theme = …` is a statement inside `gathered { … }`, so it ends when that block ends.
That is before `made_of` → `each_described` → `v.describe(...)` draws any child. With step 3a alone, a
child therefore never sees its parent's set.

F1's own example settles what "placed" means. In `form_box { button "Save" { on press {
ctx.form.submit() } } }`, the button is BUILT by the caller (before form_box sets `form`) but PLACED by
form_box's body, as `self.body`, after the set. So the frame a child is drawn under is the one in force
at the statement of the parent's body that yields it into `gathered`: not where it was built, and not
where the walk later calls it. Sets can sit between placements (`text "a"; ctx theme = dark; text
"b"`), so it is per item.

## Options
**A (recommended): `gathered` records each item's frame, and the walk enters it.**
- In a program that frames anything, a `gathered` block whose items are `dyn View`s (more generally,
  any `@placed` trait: View is marked) pushes, beside each item, the frame in force at its statement,
  into a hidden `frames` lane of the gathered record. One `avra_ctx_frame()` per placed item; nothing
  in a program with no context, so the zero-diff receipt still holds.
- std-ui's generated `describe` hands `made_of` the frames with the items. `each_described` draws item
  j under frame j through an `@std/meta` door, `placed_under(frame, () -> v.describe(...))`. It is
  lowered as the inline check plus avra_ctx_enter / back, the same IR as a framed lambda's entry, so no
  new row.
- `Frame` is an opaque `@std/meta` type, a managed pointer.
- Step 2's survey: a View item's reads are owed at its placement statement (like a lambda at its
  making), not at the walk's dyn call. That replaces rule (i)'s union for `@placed` traits only;
  `dyn Sink`, `dyn Measure` and the rest keep (i) and the caller's frame.
- **F1** follows: a handler made by the caller runs under the frame its node was drawn under. The walk
  is inside `placed_under` when the primitive's `describe` builds the Node, and the derive reframes
  each handler field that reads a context with `avra_ctx_reframed(box, frame)` (R2's row), only where
  it differs.
- **F2:** the standing keeps the frame its instance was last placed under (`Standing.frame`). A lone
  repaint enters it; an ancestor's paint refreshes it.
- **F3:** a set's value is evaluated under the paint's read tracking, so the cells it reads through
  calls become structural reads of the composition holding the set. That part is std-ui-only.

**B: no `gathered` change; std-ui wraps each item at placement into a framed lambda.** The derive
rewrites the body's bare statements `x` to `place(x)`, where `place` makes `(at) -> x.describe(at)` at
the statement. The lambda captures the frame by 3a's rule, so no new door is needed. But it rewrites
the user's body text, costs a closure per placed item in every program (no zero-cost path, because a
library unit can't know whether the program has contexts), and breaks a body that uses an item's
value.

## Asks
1. A, with `@placed` on View, and the survey owing a placed item's reads at its placement?
2. Is `placed_under` / `Frame` in `@std/meta` acceptable as the door? Its IR is 3a's entry, so there's
   no new row and no new Ins.

A fn wearing `@query` that reads a context whose type has no value to compare by is refused, whether it reads it directly or through a call. The rebuild with the final wording is still running. When it lands I'll pin the refusal case, regenerate `DIAGNOSTICS.md` and `VOICES.md`, run the gate and send the commit.

tested() {

    ran=$?
    grep '^    ✗' "$out/$name.log" | sed 's/ @ .*//; s/^    ✗ //' | sort -u >"$out/$name.failed"
    listed "tools/gate/$pkg.names" >"$out/$name.known"
    comm -23 "$out/$name.failed" "$out/$name.known" >"$out/$name.unpinned"
    grep '^avra: while running ' "$out/$name.log" | sed 's/ @ .*//; s/^avra: while running //' | sort -u >"$out/$name.trapped"
    listed "tools/gate/$pkg.traps" >"$out/$name.traps"

ctx step 4: a context a running query reads is one of its answer's reads

A `@query` answer was kept by its arguments alone, so one made under `ctx scale = 1` was handed
back under `ctx scale = 10`. A `ctx` read inside a running query body is now a dependency like a
Db read: the kernel's run opens a recording at `begin` and keeps what it heard on the cell as it
settles, and an answer is reused only while each context it heard holds what it held — by its word
(a number, a truth, a float's bits, a word enum's tag), by its text's hash, or, for a default, as no
set. A context told apart by no word (a nullable set, a record, a list) keeps no answer. A query
reused inside another is heard by it, so the outer answer moves with the inner one's context.

A read outside a query costs one load of the runtime's word and a test, as a loop's tick does; the
filing (`avra_ctx_heard`) is the cold path, out of line. The rows touch only the running task's own
state, so a query run at compile time may use them. Both engines hold it: the evaluator keeps the
recordings in a task's slot, or beside the machine while no task stands.

std-relation/src/tests/ctx_heard proves it in both engines; runtime/tests/ctx_frame_test holds the
runtime's half; the census of a program of four million context reads and no query is the same
count for count, and its time within run-to-run noise.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01QBqJumMhrCeitiL9NDC4Ui
EOF

# THE CENSUS COUNTS THE COMPILER'S OWN WORK, under a memory cap: the old path's check the net runs
# before the program layer's is not that work, and its memory with the layer's passes the cap.
export AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0
census=build/avra.census
stores=.avra-cache.census-saved
suffix=.census-saved
named="$*"
restore() {
    make --no-print-directory build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null 2>&1 || \
        echo "census: the shipping runtime did NOT rebuild — run \`make build/libavra_runtime.a\`"
    rm -f packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll
    if [ -d "$stores" ]; then rm -rf .avra-cache; mv "$stores" .avra-cache; fi
    for d in $named; do
        if [ -d "$d/.avra-cache$suffix" ]; then rm -rf "$d/.avra-cache"; mv "$d/.avra-cache$suffix" "$d/.avra-cache"; fi
    done
}
trap restore EXIT INT TERM

rm -rf "$stores"
[ -d .avra-cache ] && mv .avra-cache "$stores"
sh tools/census_compiler.sh "$census"

# THE MEASURED RUN STARTS COLD: the census compiler's store is its own
# and was never filled, and the tree's stores stand aside until exit.
# THE FILTER DROPS `mem:`, IT DOES NOT SELECT LABELS: an allowlist of
# census labels is a second registry of them, and goes stale silently.
# A PACKAGE NAMED ON THE COMMAND KEEPS ITS OWN STORE (`tapes <pkg>` writes `<pkg>/.avra-cache`), so it
# stands aside too, or the second census of one package reads the first one's answers.
rm -rf .avra-cache
for d in "$@"; do
    if [ -d "$d/.avra-cache" ]; then rm -rf "$d/.avra-cache$suffix"; mv "$d/.avra-cache" "$d/.avra-cache$suffix"; fi
done
if [ -n "${CENSUS_EDIT:-}" ]; then
    sh tools/memcap.sh "${CENSUS_CAP_MB:-4000}" "$census" "$@" > build/census-cold.out 2>&1 || { tail -5 build/census-cold.out; echo "census: the cold run failed"; exit 1; }
    sh -c "$CENSUS_EDIT"
fi
out="$(AVRA_MEM_STATS=1 AVRA_CENSUS_SITES=1 sh tools/memcap.sh "${CENSUS_CAP_MB:-4000}" "$census" "$@" 2>&1 >/dev/null \
    | tee build/census-raw.out | grep -Ev '^(mem:|memcap:)' || true)"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q '^rc:' || { printf '%s\n' "$out" | tail -5; echo "census: the run printed no counts"; exit 1; }

# THE STORE'S BYTES, read while the census run's own store stands (the exit trap puts the tree's
# back): a row ceiling alone misses rows that got larger.
python3 - <<'PY' > build/census-store.out 2>/dev/null || true
import os
n = 0
for d, _, files in os.walk(".avra-cache/store"):
    n += sum(os.path.getsize(os.path.join(d, f)) for f in files)
print("store: %d bytes" % n)
PY
out="$out
$(cat build/census-store.out 2>/dev/null)"

# Every site's symbol, one line per address in the order given: `atos` on macOS, `addr2line`
# elsewhere, each asked ONCE for all of them — a table of thousands of sites asked one at a time
# spends longer resolving than the census spent counting.
symbols_at() {
    if command -v atos > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        xargs atos -o "$census" 2>/dev/null
    else
        xargs addr2line -f -e "$census" 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR % 2 == 1'
    fi

#!/bin/sh
# THE CENSUS BUILD: exact retain/release/list-write counts, and the
# callers that cause them. Counting costs ~8% of a run, so it never
# ships: a census compiler is built BESIDE build/avra, from a runtime
# compiled with -DAVRA_CENSUS, and the shipping runtime library is
# rebuilt on every exit.
#   sh tools/census.sh check packages/std-avrac
#
# THE SHIPPING COMPILER IS NEVER REMOVED. It builds the census
# compiler, so a census that deletes it first has nothing to build
# with, and every recovery that rebuilds needs the memory and disk the
# census run just spent.
#
# CENSUS_EDIT MEASURES A WARM EDIT: the command runs once cold to fill the store,
# then CENSUS_EDIT edits the tree, and only the run after it is counted.
#   CENSUS_EDIT='sh tools/db_measure/edit_literal.sh' sh tools/census.sh check packages/cli
#
# A CENSUS THAT PRINTS NO COUNTS FAILS. A check that examined nothing
# is not a check that passed: no `rc:` line means the binary carried no
# census, and the run exits 1 saying so.
# A cold run clears the tree's `.avra-cache`; the machine store lives there too, or "cold" would read the machine's rows.
export AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)/.avra-cache"
# a store is copied, counted or emptied here between builds, so each build saves its own before it answers
export AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
: "${LLVM_PREFIX:=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm}"
export LLVM_PREFIX

# THE CENSUS COUNTS THE COMPILER'S OWN WORK, under a memory cap: the old path's check the net runs

# callers that cause them. Counting costs ~8% of a run, so it never

content.text: Ruled (c), with a cost condition: outside a running query, a context read checks one word and nothing more; the recording is the cold path, out of line. First, how a `ctx` read lowers today:

message.content: Lead: (c). A context read inside a query body is a dependency like a Db read: one mechanism, exact on every path. Condition (P4): outside a running query the hook costs nothing measurable. A ctx read checks one "inside a query" word and does nothing else; the recording is the cold path, out of line. Show the census on a ctx-heavy program without queries, before and after. Witness: your ctx_query_stale package answers 20 under `ctx scale = 10` and 2 outside it, in both engines, plus one case where a cached answer is reused because the context held the same value.

payload.result:
I've started ctx step 4 (cached-fn keys), but I'm holding the build for the lead's choice of design.

The bug is real. A `@query` answer is keyed by its arguments only, so it outlives the context it read. The repro is at `/work/asks-back/ctx_query_stale`: under `ctx scale = 10`, `scaled(db, 2)` answers 2 instead of 20.

My first plan had a phase problem. The compiler only learns which contexts a fn reads after lowering, but `@query`'s derive runs before that, so it can't add those values to the key. The two ways left:
- **(c), my lean: record at runtime.** The query engine records each `ctx` read made inside a query body as a dependency, as it already does for Db reads. A kept answer then stands only while the context holds the same values. It's exact on every path and needs no derive change, but it needs a hook from the context read into the running query.
- **(a'): a syntax-level read set for derives.** The derive walks the body and the callees it resolves to. It's exact on direct calls but duplicates the compiler's own read survey.

The repro stays outside the test tree until the fix lands; a known-failing test would break the suite. Item 3 is still held until batch 58's head arrives, when I'll check `tab` against layer-commands' head-field rule.

content.content:
Settled in the design review of 2026-11-18 (the lane's design: `avra-lane-ui-language-ctx.md`):

- **The value is a frame on the task**: one entry per declared `ctx`; a set copies the frame, a read
  is one load. A caught trap puts the guard's frame back by one store.
- **A change repaints by structure.** What a set's value reads are structural reads of the
  composition holding the set, so a write repaints that subtree whole; an exact patch never shows a
  stale context value. A child repainting alone runs under the frame its instance was drawn under.
- **A handler on a node runs under the frame the node was drawn under**, as a view does; a plain
  closure or a fn value keeps the frame where it was made.
- **The required check is sound through `dyn` calls**: a `dyn T` call counts as reading every `ctx`
  any impl of `T` reads (relayed by the compiler lead as the owner's ruling; measured: no refusal
  added on std-ui or the board). It runs at entries; `explain` shows an exported fn's reads.
- **A cached fn reads only a `ctx` that compares by value**; its key adds each read's value. One
  holding fns or cells is refused inside a cached fn.
- **No implicit default**: `ctx x: T? = null` is written out. `theme`'s default is the target's own
  default theme. A `ctx` is imported by name and shares the top-level namespace.

Owed before it is built, each as a real program: a cache keyed by a fn's inputs counts its
context reads; "this fn reads `db`" computed lazily, so a deep edit does not ripple through every
caller; a trap caught by a guard restores the context (on wasm a caught trap runs no cleanup
today); a lint against a context where a parameter would do.

The prior art read was Odin and Jai

Lead:
A) Merge: 10daeba0 conflicts with batch 57's current head in compiler/item_context_reads.av (57 has moved on since land57: laws-fusion's reads_view and parity-values). Rather than chase a moving head, you ride batch 58: when 57 lands I'll send its head, you merge, and you send 57..HEAD.

1. `@seeds`: DROP. The derive's law becomes "a primitive member that projects nothing AND that no member's default reads is refused". `initial` stands because `value`'s default reads it.
2. `@over(value)`: KEEP. (a) Its argument must name a `state` member of the same component whose type is the marked member's T under T?, refused at the declaration otherwise. 3. `@sets(place)` / `@sets(place, constant)`: KEEP. (a) The one-argument form requires the event to carry exactly one payload of the place's type, refused otherwise; a constant must fit the place's type. (b) The write lands before the caller's handler on every target, with a test that a handlerless `field` keeps what was typed. (c) Several events may set one place, each marked.
4. All marks are the primitive derive's vocabulary: on a component without `@prim` they are refused, never silently inert.
5. The control re-asserts `shown` after a gesture on every target.

cd /work/avra && git add -A docs/2026_11_16_UI.md packages/std-ui/src tools/ui-board/src/board.av && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
std-ui: a field, a checkbox and a dialog keep a place, and are held to what is shown

Each control's value is a `state` member: given a place it shares it (`field "Name" { value:
draft }`), given none the instance first built where it stands is kept, seeded from `initial`; a
value handed it is refused, as any `state` seat refuses one. The control's gesture writes the
place before its handler hears it, so a handlerless field keeps what is typed. `shown: T?` is told
each paint and never written: the node shows `shown ?? value`, so headless, the terminal and the
DOM page (written back where it holds otherwise) are held to it, and the HTML a page is first
served carries it.

The derive reads three marks for it: `@seeds(value)` on the member the place starts from,
`@over(value)` on what is shown in its place, `@sets(value)` on the event that writes it
(`@sets(open, false)` for one that says nothing). A primitive's kept place stands as a
composition's does (`stood`, a `Kept` seat), its spread fields carried each paint. A kept place no
event sets is refused, in new words.

Callers that passed a value now pass `shown:` (the program's truth, unchanged behaviour); the
boards' redundant draft and dismiss handlers go. A field always names its value now, so the
screens that read `field "n" placeholder=""` read `value=""` too.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01QBqJumMhrCeitiL9NDC4Ui
EOF

  (`field "Name" { value: draft }`), given none they keep their own, seeded from `initial`; a value

  old shape.
'''

EOF

#!/bin/sh
# THE BOARD IN A REAL BROWSER: tools/ui-board served by `avra dev` and
# driven in headless Firefox by
# tools/ui-board/browser.mjs, which checks each claim and exits 1 on the
# first that fails. `make ui-board` proves the wire over a stub document;
# this proves what only an engine can — and the dev loop: the view's file is
# edited and the running page must follow.
#
# It needs what `make ui-board` needs, Firefox (and, where it is asked for, Playwright's WebKit) (FIREFOX names one that is
# not in a usual place). Where one is absent this FAILS, naming what is
# missing: a run that examined nothing is no pass. Only a hand-set
# UI_BROWSER_SKIP=<reason> stands it down on a local machine, loudly; on the
# checks' machine (CI=true) nothing does. UI_BOARD_TARGET names one wasm triple (default `wasm`);
# UI_BROWSER_SHOTS names a directory the run leaves screenshots in. UI_BROWSER_ENGINES names the engines
# to run, in order (default `firefox`; the checks name `firefox webkit`); UI_BROWSER_DEVICE names a Playwright device
# ("iPhone 15") for the WebKit run: a touch screen and a phone's window.
set -eu

# Whether a browser stands at the path `$1`.
webkit_stands() { [ -e "$1" ]; }

# THE PATH THE LAUNCHER RUNS, as Playwright's own module names it: the guard
# and the launch read one answer, so no cache can stand for a browser it lacks.
webkit_exe() {
    PW_PREFIX=$1 node --input-type=module -e 'const { webkit } = await import(process.env.PW_PREFIX + "/node_modules/playwright/index.mjs"); process.stdout.write(webkit.executablePath());'
}

# `--self-test`: both surfaces of the skip contract, run against a compiler that
# is not there (the first thing a run needs), so no browser is touched.
if [ "${1:-}" = --self-test ]; then
    me=$0
    ran() { env -u CI -u UI_BROWSER_SKIP AVRA=/nonexistent "$@" sh "$me" 2>&1; }
    out=$(ran) && { echo "ui-browser self-test: a missing machine passed"; exit 1; }
    case $out in *UI_BROWSER_SKIP*) ;; *) echo "ui-browser self-test: the refusal does not name its opt-out"; exit 1;; esac
    out=$(ran UI_BROWSER_SKIP=no-firefox-here) || { echo "ui-browser self-test: UI_BROWSER_SKIP did not stand it down"; exit 1; }
    case $out in *"STOOD DOWN"*no-firefox-here*) ;; *) echo "ui-browser self-test: a stand-down is not spoken with its reason"; exit 1;; esac
    out=$(env CI=true UI_BROWSER_SKIP=no-firefox-here AVRA=/nonexistent sh "$me" 2>&1) && { echo "ui-browser self-test: CI stood down"; exit 1; }
    # BOTH SURFACES OF THE GUARD, asked of a Playwright module that names its
    # own executable: a path with a browser is read as standing, and a path
    # with none is read as missing — the case a restored cache used to pass at
    # once, and the reason a cache is validated rather than assumed.
    command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "ui-browser self-test: no \`node\` to ask Playwright's module"; exit 1; }
    d=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/avra-webkit-guard.XXXXXX")
    mkdir -p "$d/module/node_modules/playwright" "$d/standing"
    printf '%s\n' 'export const webkit = { executablePath: () => process.env.PW_ANSWER };' >"$d/module/node_modules/playwright/index.mjs"
    : >"$d/standing/pw_run.sh"
    if [ "$(PW_ANSWER="$d/standing/pw_run.sh" webkit_exe "$d/module")" != "$d/standing/pw_run.sh" ]; then
        echo "ui-browser self-test: the guard did not read the launcher's own answer"
        find "$d" -delete
        exit 1
    fi
    if webkit_stands "$(PW_ANSWER="$d/gone/pw_run.sh" webkit_exe "$d/module")"; then
        echo "ui-browser self-test: a path with no browser was read as standing"
        find "$d" -delete
        exit 1
    fi
    find "$d" -delete
    echo "ui-browser self-test: a missing machine fails, only UI_BROWSER_SKIP stands it down, CI never does; the guard reads the path the launcher names"
    exit 0
fi

3	//! `@derive(View)` WRITES that impl. A component that names a primitive
4	//! (`@prim`) is one, drawn from what each member SAYS it projects to:
5	//!
6	//!     @attr(.Label) label: string     an attribute of the node
7	//!     @attr(.Value) value: string?    one the node names only when given
8	//!     @children items: List<dyn View> the node's children

11	//!     ..Box                           the shared box, read field for field
12	//!
13	//! NO MEANING IS READ FROM A MEMBER'S NAME: a member that says nothing is
14	//! refused where it stands. Every word a member says is checked against
15	//! the library's own declaration — a primitive against `Prim`, an
16	//! attribute against `Attribute`, a style against `Style`, what an event
17	//! says against `Handler` — so each fact has the one table its type
18	//! already is, and a word or a type that does not fit is refused at the
19	//! member, never inside this file. An event names no target: each target's

content.content:
`ctx theme`, the Crisp look as theme data, and its claims hold. No further study opens before it.

An earlier ten-stage outline of the 652 planned or partly built ideas (finish what stands; screens
and navigation; core components; data on the device; actions and forms; theme, accessibility and
motion; assets; dev tooling; more targets; agents and security) is the ledger's content by stage;
the studies above set the order.

## Authoring: decisions

Owner decisions of 2026-11-17, from the component authoring study. A component here is any
component (a queue, a command, a server), not only a UI one.

- **A component's own names are read through `self.`**, as today: head props, fields and
  state are `self.x`, and what stands outside the component is bare, so a reader tells the
  two apart at sight. Rejected: all bare (decided and withdrawn the same day; it hides which
  names are the component's); a leading dot, `.x` (it is the spelling of an enum variant,
  `shows: .All`).
- **A place is passed with no marker.** A seat declared `state` takes the caller's place:
  `stepper count`, `field "Name" { value: draft }`. Passing what is no place is a compile
  error at the call. Rejected: a call-site sigil (SwiftUI's `$x`, Svelte's `bind:`), since
  `state` fn parameters already take `stepper(c)` bare.
- **`state` stands in a component head**, as it does in a fn's parameters.
- **`state` always means a place** (owner 2026-11-18). A place is a `state` binding (local, module
  or seat) or a `state` field by any path (`self.draft`, `t.title`); a `state` field holds a Cell a
  copy of its record shares. A member `state x: T = d` given a place shares it; given nothing, the
  instance keeps its own. A value passed to `state` is a compile error, with no exception for a
  literal. A seed is an ordinary input the member's default reads once:

  ```avra
  component counter(start: int = 0) { state n: int = self.start }
  counter { start: 10 }     // seeded
  counter { n: count }      // shared
  counter { n: 10 }         // refused
  ```

  Rejected: a value seeds and a place shares under one spelling (`field { value: t.title }` over a
  plain field compiles and never saves); the same with a guard that refuses a changeable name (a
  rule the reader cannot see). Unbuilt: a member default reading a prop. Not solved here, for the
  state-and-sync study: a place through a `state` list of plain records (`todos[i].title`), and a
  place made of a read and a write.
- **A slot is a field of views, and one slot may be the default.** A composition's field of
  type `List<dyn View>` is a slot: no keyword, no slot-only mark. `@default`, the mark that
  already names a component's default event, may stand on one slot instead; a component has
  one default, an event or a slot, and a block's bare content fills it. Every other slot is
  filled by a block under its name. Rejected: a `slot` keyword and `@children` on a
  composition (a second spelling of what a typed field already says); "the first slot is the
  default" (a rule the reader cannot see).

  ```avra
  component panel(title: string) {
      @default body: List<dyn View> = []
      actions: List<dyn View> = []
      column {
          heading self.title
          self.body
          row { self.actions }
      }
  }

  panel "Settings" {
      toggle dense
      actions { button "Done" {} }
  }
  ```

  Unbuilt: `@default` on a field is refused ("only an event can be a component's default"),
  and a slot takes `actions: collect { … }`, not `actions { … }`.
- **A key is any comparable value**: `key: t.id`, not `key: "${t.id}"`.
- **`words` and `reads` leave every primitive**: the derive that needs them adds them.
- **An event names no target.** A component declares `on press`; each target's own table maps
  it to a click, a key or a tap (ruled 2026-10-18).

# THE COMPILER BUILDS ITSELF. `build/avra` is the working binary and
# `make avra` rebuilds it with the binary already there; a cold tree
# bootstraps from the seed (`make bootstrap`, or `./avra` on its own).
# What links what:
#   build/llvm_wrapper.o  OURS — backend/llvm_wrapper.c, the
#                         compiler's LLVM binding; new builders are
#                         added there, never hunted for upstream.
#   build/libavra_runtime.a  OURS — runtime/*.c, the native half of
#                         the LANGUAGE's semantics, one object per
#                         file; the only runtime avra-built programs
#                         link. A LIBRARY, so a program links only the
#                         objects it reaches: one that never spawns
#                         carries no scheduler.
#   build/<stem>.o        A PACKAGE'S — its C under src/c/, or a
#                         vendored unit under vendor/, named by its
#                         manifest's [link].
# ONE RULE builds all of them, the two above included: every object in
# this tree comes from `build/%.o: %.c` and from nowhere else.

# The default is one of two copies: `LLVM_PREFIXES` in packages/cli/src/commands/shared.av
# holds the compiler's own, since this builds before any compiler exists.
LLVM_PREFIX ?= /opt/homebrew/opt/llvm
# a manifest's link flags name it as ${LLVM_PREFIX}
export LLVM_PREFIX
# An archive is its members alone, never the hour it was made: a check reads it as an
# input, so two checkouts' archives must be the same bytes (macOS `ar` stamps the clock).
export ZERO_AR_DATE = 1
# A TARGET REPLACES, COPIES AND EMPTIES WHAT A BUILD JUST WROTE — the compiler a build ran from, the
# stores it saved — so every build `make` runs saves its store before it answers, leaving no heir
# running the binary a recipe is about to replace.
export AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE = 1
# THE C++ RUNTIME AND THE SYSTEM LIBRARY DIRECTORY the static LLVM link names
# (packages/std-avrac/avra.toml), per platform.
ifeq ($(shell uname -s),Darwin)
export AVRA_CXX_RUNTIME ?= c++
export AVRA_SYS_SEARCH ?= /opt/homebrew/lib
else
export AVRA_CXX_RUNTIME ?= stdc++
endif
# THE COMPILER'S LLVM LINK, one definition: the manifest row, read by the
# hand-written clang lines below so none of them spells the libraries again.
LLVM_LINK := $(shell sh tools/llvm_link.sh --words)

# The objects the COMPILER itself links: the runtime every program
# carries, and the compiler's own foreign machinery (the LLVM wrapper,
# the evaluator's extern trampoline), which no user program does. The
# name says COMPILER because that is what it is — a user's binary
# links build/libavra_runtime.a and nothing else here. The compiler
# links every runtime OBJECT whole, since the evaluator hosts every
# row whether or not the compiler's own code calls it.
#
# ONE LIST, NOT TWO. The bootstrap's clang line spells its inputs, and
# spelling them twice is a law waiting to disagree with itself: the
# trampoline was added to one and not the other, and the seed-built
# compiler would have failed to link the day the seed was refreshed.
#
# THIS IS WHAT THE BOOTSTRAP LINKS BY HAND, NOT WHAT THE COMPILER'S
# BUILD NEEDS ON DISK. `make avra` runs `./avra build packages/cli`,
# which links every `[link]` object in that package's dependency
# closure — @std/io's among them — so a build that depended on this
# list alone fails on a tree where the package's object was never
# made. It did, twice: once for the trampoline and once for @std/io's
# own C. So each target depends on WHAT IT LINKS, and the two lists
# below are that split.

# EVERY OBJECT THIS TREE COMPILES, ONE RULE. The language's own C
# (runtime/, and the compiler's LLVM binding in backend/) and a
# package's C — its own under src/c/, a vendored translation unit
# under vendor/ — all compile to build/<stem>.o, and a package's
# manifest names that object in its [link]: A MANIFEST SAYS WHAT TO
# LINK, NEVER HOW TO BUILD IT, and this rule is the how
# (docs/2026_09_07_PACKAGE_C_STANDARD.md). The sources are GLOBBED,
# never listed — a hand-written list forgets its next member, and
# build/sqlite3.o had no rule at all for a day — so a new package's C
# is built without a line here. ONE HOW FOR EVERY OBJECT is the point:
# a hand-written rule beside the pattern SHADOWS it (make prefers the
# explicit one), so a package source named avra_runtime.c was compiled
# by nobody while its manifest linked the runtime. Our own C is held
# to -Wall -Werror; a vendored unit takes its author's flags
# (CFLAGS_<stem>) and no warning of ours.
TREE_C := $(wildcard packages/*/src/c/*.c packages/*/vendor/*.c backend/*.c runtime/*.c runtime/host/*.c)
vpath %.c $(sort $(dir $(TREE_C)))

# A STEM NAMES ITS OBJECT, so a stem is UNIQUE TREE-WIDE. One flat
# build/ holds every object and vpath answers the FIRST directory
# carrying a name, so two packages with a src/c/util.c compile ONE of
# them and the other's manifest links an object built from someone
# else's source. The law is named HERE because the link cannot name
# it: it fails on a symbol that does exist in the tree, in a file
# nothing ever compiled. Make expands a rule's prerequisites as it
# READS them, so a clash refuses every target, `clean` included —
# nothing but renaming a file fixes it anyway. tools/stems.sh drives
# these lines with synthetic sources; there is no second copy.
#
# AND THE COMPARISON FOLDS CASE, because `build/` is a DIRECTORY and
# not a set of names: on the volumes this tree builds on it does not
# tell `util.o` from `Util.o`, so `a/util.c` beside `b/Util.c` has
# distinct spellings and ONE object. Proved rather than argued — both
# compiled, `build/Casestem.o` was never a separate file, and
# `build/casestem.o` carried the other package's symbol, with the law
# reporting the tree fine. The clash is read in ONE pass that answers
# the FILES, so nothing has to search a folded stem back to its
# spelling; groups come out ordered by that stem, since an awk map's
# own order must never reach output.
TREE_CLASH := $(strip $(shell printf '%s\n' $(TREE_C) \
  | awk -F/ '{ s = tolower($$NF); sub(/\.c$$/, "", s); n[s]++; f[s] = f[s] " " $$0 } \
              END { for (s in n) if (n[s] > 1) print s "\t" f[s] }' \
  | sort | cut -f2))
TREE_STEM_LAW = $(if $(TREE_CLASH),$(error A STEM NAMES ITS OBJECT, \
  so a stem is unique tree-wide — one flat `build/` holds every object \
  and does not tell `u.c` from `U.c` — rename one of: $(TREE_CLASH)))

# A TARGET DEPENDS ON WHAT IT LINKS, AND ON NOTHING ELSE. Two lists,
# because there are two kinds of link and one list served neither
# well: depending on every object made `make avra` compile the 9.5 MB
# vendored amalgamation for a binary that never links it, and
# depending on a hand-kept list let `make avra` link an object it had
# never built — twice, the trampoline and then @std/io's own C.
#
# COMPILER_OBJS is what `build/avra` itself links: the runtime every
# program carries, plus every object a manifest names in the cli's
# closure — the cli and each @std package its sources `use`, asked of
# tools/manifest_objects.sh, the one reader of a `[link]` row. The
# bootstrap's clang line takes this same variable, so the two can never
# be a list and its copy. A package object in the compiler's own closure
# (@std/io's: a compiler that cannot open a file cannot compile the tree)
# is BOTH a package object and a compiler one, and joins here the day its
# package's `use` lands. An archive brings its members (MEMBERS_<name>),
# which a seed links in its place.
# The runtime's objects are GLOBBED, one per runtime/*.c, so a new
# runtime file joins the library without a line here.
RUNTIME_OBJS = $(patsubst runtime/%.c,build/%.o,$(wildcard runtime/*.c)) build/avra_tick.o
RUNTIME_LIB = build/libavra_runtime.a

COMPILER_PACKAGE_OBJS := $(shell sh tools/manifest_objects.sh --closure cli)
COMPILER_ARCHIVES = $(filter %.a,$(COMPILER_PACKAGE_OBJS))
COMPILER_OBJS = $(TREE_STEM_LAW)$(RUNTIME_OBJS) $(RUNTIME_LIB) $(COMPILER_PACKAGE_OBJS) \
                $(foreach a,$(COMPILER_ARCHIVES),$(MEMBERS_$(notdir $(a))))

# A seed names an archive's rows itself, so its link takes them once: the members, not also their archive.
SEED_LINK_OBJS = $(filter-out $(COMPILER_ARCHIVES),$(COMPILER_OBJS))

# PACKAGE_OBJS is every object a package's `[link]` row names — what a
# target that RUNS programs may need, since any package's suite or
# program tests can link its own C.
PACKAGE_OBJS := $(TREE_STEM_LAW)$(shell sh tools/manifest_objects.sh)

# PER-OBJECT FLAGS, by stem. The LLVM binding needs its headers; the
# vendored amalgamation takes its author's whole flag set, which its
# own suite asks the LIBRARY to confirm.
CFLAGS_avra_tick := -Iruntime
CFLAGS_llvm_wrapper := -I$(LLVM_PREFIX)/include
CFLAGS_ffi := -Iruntime
CFLAGS_std_io := -Iruntime
CFLAGS_sqlite3 = $(SQLITE_FLAGS)
CFLAGS_sqlite_sentinel := -Ipackages/std-sqlite/vendor

# THE VENDORED mbedTLS, ONE OBJECT PER UPSTREAM UNIT: each
# packages/std-tls/vendor/mbedtls_<unit>.c wrapper includes one upstream
# .c, so every unit compiles as upstream compiles it (a unity build lets
# one unit's macros reach the next). They are ARCHIVED with @std/tls's
# own C, so a program links the members it reaches and no more — one
# that only signs links no handshake. The two config headers in src/c
# are the whole mechanism list; @std/tls's own C reads mbedTLS's
# structs, so it compiles under the same words.
MBEDTLS_DIR := packages/std-tls/vendor/mbedtls
MBEDTLS_OBJS := $(patsubst packages/std-tls/vendor/%.c,build/%.o,$(wildcard packages/std-tls/vendor/mbedtls_*.c))
MBEDTLS_FLAGS := -I$(MBEDTLS_DIR)/include -I$(MBEDTLS_DIR)/tf-psa-crypto/include \
  -I$(MBEDTLS_DIR)/tf-psa-crypto/drivers/builtin/include -I$(MBEDTLS_DIR)/library \
  -I$(MBEDTLS_DIR)/tf-psa-crypto/core -I$(MBEDTLS_DIR)/tf-psa-crypto/dispatch \
  -I$(MBEDTLS_DIR)/tf-psa-crypto/drivers/builtin/src -I$(MBEDTLS_DIR)/tf-psa-crypto/extras \
  -I$(MBEDTLS_DIR)/tf-psa-crypto/platform -I$(MBEDTLS_DIR)/tf-psa-crypto/utilities \
  -I$(MBEDTLS_DIR)/tf-psa-crypto/drivers/everest/include \
  -I$(MBEDTLS_DIR)/tf-psa-crypto/drivers/everest/include/tf-psa-crypto/private/everest \
  -I$(MBEDTLS_DIR)/tf-psa-crypto/drivers/everest/include/tf-psa-crypto/private/everest/kremlib \
  -Ipackages/std-tls/src/c '-DTF_PSA_CRYPTO_CONFIG_FILE="std_tls_crypto_config.h"' \
  '-DMBEDTLS_CONFIG_FILE="std_tls_ssl_config.h"'
TLS_OBJS := $(patsubst packages/std-tls/src/c/%.c,build/%.o,$(wildcard packages/std-tls/src/c/*.c)) $(MBEDTLS_OBJS)
$(foreach o,$(TLS_OBJS),$(eval CFLAGS_$(basename $(notdir $(o))) := $(MBEDTLS_FLAGS)))

MEMBERS_std_tls.a = $(TLS_OBJS)
build/std_tls.a: $(MEMBERS_std_tls.a)
	@rm -f $@
	ar rcs $@ $^

# THE VENDORED zlib AND brotli, one object per upstream unit
# (packages/std-compress/vendor/import.sh writes the wrappers),
# ARCHIVED with @std/compress's own C as TLS's are: a program links the
# members it reaches, and a program that never compresses links none.
# brotli's units and @std/compress's C read brotli's public headers by
# their installed name.
BROTLI_INCLUDE := -Ipackages/std-compress/vendor/brotli/include
COMPRESS_OBJS := build/std_compress.o $(patsubst packages/std-compress/vendor/%.c,build/%.o,$(wildcard packages/std-compress/vendor/zlib_*.c packages/std-compress/vendor/brotli_*.c))
$(foreach o,$(filter build/brotli_%,$(COMPRESS_OBJS)),$(eval CFLAGS_$(basename $(notdir $(o))) := $(BROTLI_INCLUDE)))
CFLAGS_std_compress := -Ipackages/std-compress/vendor $(BROTLI_INCLUDE)

MEMBERS_std_compress.a = $(COMPRESS_OBJS)
build/std_compress.a: $(MEMBERS_std_compress.a)
	@rm -f $@
	ar rcs $@ $^

# THE VENDORED BLAKE3, one object per upstream unit
# (packages/std-hash/vendor/import.sh writes the wrappers), ARCHIVED
# with @std/hash's own C. Only this machine's SIMD units are built, each
# under the flags its intrinsics need, and blake3_dispatch asks the CPU
# at run time which of them to run; any other machine runs the portable
# unit alone.
HASH_ARCH := $(shell uname -m)
B3_SIMD := $(if $(filter arm64 aarch64,$(HASH_ARCH)),neon,$(if $(filter x86_64 amd64,$(HASH_ARCH)),sse2 sse41 avx2 avx512))
HASH_OBJS := build/std_hash.o $(patsubst %,build/b3_%.o,blake3 blake3_dispatch blake3_portable $(addprefix blake3_,$(B3_SIMD)))
$(foreach o,$(HASH_OBJS),$(eval CFLAGS_$(basename $(notdir $(o))) := -Ipackages/std-hash/vendor))
CFLAGS_b3_blake3_sse2 += -msse2
CFLAGS_b3_blake3_sse41 += -msse4.1
CFLAGS_b3_blake3_avx2 += -mavx2
CFLAGS_b3_blake3_avx512 += -mavx512f -mavx512vl

MEMBERS_std_hash.a = $(HASH_OBJS)
build/std_hash.a: $(MEMBERS_std_hash.a)
	@rm -f $@
	ar rcs $@ $^

# THE HASHER'S DOOR, FORGED: @std/hash takes a hasher's state back as a
# value, so forged states are pushed through it with the package's C
# rebuilt under ASan and UBSan, each unit under its own flags. A machine
# whose compiler carries no sanitizer runtime says so and runs nothing.
HASH_DOOR_SAN := -g -O1 -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all
hash-door: packages/std-hash/src/c/tests/door_test.c $(HASH_OBJS)
	@mkdir -p build/hash-door
	@if ! { printf 'int main(void) { return 0; }\n' | cc $(HASH_DOOR_SAN) -x c - -o build/hash-door/probe 2>/dev/null && build/hash-door/probe; }; then \
	  echo "hash-door: ASan unavailable — not run"; \
	else \
	  $(foreach o,$(HASH_OBJS),cc -c $(HASH_DOOR_SAN) $(CFLAGS_$(basename $(notdir $(o)))) -o build/hash-door/$(notdir $(o)) $(if $(filter build/std_hash.o,$(o)),packages/std-hash/src/c/std_hash.c,packages/std-hash/vendor/$(basename $(notdir $(o))).c) &&) \
	  cc $(HASH_DOOR_SAN) -Ipackages/std-hash/vendor -o build/hash-door/door_test $< $(addprefix build/hash-door/,$(notdir $(HASH_OBJS))) && \
	  build/hash-door/door_test; \
	fi

# A HEADER IS A SOURCE. cc writes each object's dependency list beside
# it and the next make reads it back, so editing a .h rebuilds what
# includes it — without this a package that grows a header links a
# stale object and the defect is attributed to the compiler. The
# include is silent on a cold tree, where no .d exists yet.
# A FRAME NEVER SKIPS A GUARD: code that may run on a task's stack
# probes a frame wider than a page, a page at a time. Apple's clang
# does so by default (___chkstk_darwin); elsewhere it is asked for.
STACK_PROBES := $(if $(filter Darwin,$(shell uname -s)),,-fstack-clash-protection)
# A PROGRAM CARRIES WHAT IT REACHES: every C function and datum stands in a
# section of its own, so a link that drops unreached sections drops it.
# AVRA_FRAME_POINTERS=1 keeps frame pointers in the runtime and, read by the backend, in every
# emitted fn, so a sampling profiler can walk Avra stacks. Off, nothing changes.
SECTIONS := -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections $(if $(AVRA_FRAME_POINTERS),-fno-omit-frame-pointer)

build/%.o: %.c build/%.sha
	@mkdir -p build
	cc -c -O2 -fPIC -MMD -MP $(STACK_PROBES) $(SECTIONS) $(if $(findstring /vendor/,$<),,-Wall -Werror) $(CFLAGS_$*) -o $@ $<

-include $(patsubst %.o,%.d,$(filter %.o,$(sort $(COMPILER_OBJS) $(PACKAGE_OBJS) $(TLS_OBJS) $(COMPRESS_OBJS) $(HASH_OBJS))))

# THE HOT LEAVES AS BYTES THE COMPILER CARRIES (runtime/avra_hot.h):
# runtime/avra_hot.c compiled to bitcode by the LLVM the compiler links,
# then written into backend/llvm_wrapper.c's include, so every module can
# inline the leaves and the compiler's own digest covers them — a changed
# leaf retires every cached object. An LLVM without clang carries none,
# and the leaves stay calls. THE LEAVES MAY UNWIND (-fexceptions): a trap inside
# one, inlined under a call with a cleanup region open, reaches that region.
build/avra_hot.bc: runtime/avra_hot.c runtime/avra_hot.h runtime/avra_box.h
	@mkdir -p build
	@if [ -x $(LLVM_PREFIX)/bin/clang ]; then $(LLVM_PREFIX)/bin/clang -c -emit-llvm -O2 -fPIC -fexceptions -Iruntime -o $@ runtime/avra_hot.c; else rm -f $@; touch $@; fi

build/avra_hot.inc: build/avra_hot.bc
	@python3 -c "import sys; d=open(sys.argv[1],'rb').read(); print('static const unsigned char avra_hot_bc[] = {' + (','.join(str(b) for b in d) or '0') + '};'); print('static const unsigned long avra_hot_bc_len = %d;' % len(d))" $< > $@

build/llvm_wrapper.o: build/avra_hot.inc

# The library is REBUILT WHOLE from its objects, never updated in
# place: a member dropped from runtime/ must not linger in it.
$(RUNTIME_LIB): $(RUNTIME_OBJS)
	@rm -f $@
	@ar rcs $@ $^

# THE RUNTIME AS WEBASSEMBLY, one object per file, MINUS the one that has no
# wasm body: a core forks, and wasm cannot. The scheduler is IN, hosted: its
# tasks run on stacks the host makes (JSPI, or asyncify), so its OS halves —
# stacks, poller, signals, the case runner — are compiled out
# (runtime/avra_fiber.c, AVRA_HOSTED). Excluding the core HERE makes the law
# structural rather than a hope, and a program links only the members it
# reaches in any case.
# THE WASM TOOLCHAIN IS FOUND, by the rule the compiler finds it by
# (packages/cli/src/commands/shared.av, `wasm_tools`): the clang `LLVM_PREFIX`
# names when it has one, else the PATH's; and the first triple that clang has
# a WASI libc for — where it says the target's startup object stands is a file.
# The archiver is that LLVM's too: a host `ar` that does not know a wasm
# object writes an archive with no index, and the link finds nothing in it.
WASM_TRIPLES := wasm32-unknown-wasi wasm32-wasip1
WASM_CC ?= $(firstword $(wildcard $(LLVM_PREFIX)/bin/clang) clang)
WASM_TARGET ?= $(firstword $(foreach t,$(WASM_TRIPLES),$(if $(wildcard $(shell $(WASM_CC) --target=$(t) -print-file-name=crt1.o 2>/dev/null)),$(t))) $(firstword $(WASM_TRIPLES)))
WASM_AR ?= $(firstword $(wildcard $(LLVM_PREFIX)/bin/llvm-ar) ar)
WASI_SYSROOT ?=
WASM_EMULATED := -D_WASI_EMULATED_MMAN -D_WASI_EMULATED_SIGNAL -D_WASI_EMULATED_GETPID
# A MODULE CARRIES NO INSTRUMENTS: the page and the node runner hand a module
# no environment to switch one on with, and a wasm frame has no return address
# for one to name a site by. `make -B WASM_INSTRUMENTS=1 wasm-runtime` builds
# the archive with them, for a host that passes an environment.
WASM_INSTRUMENTS ?= 0
# A GUARDED RUN CATCHES A TRAP IN PLACE: the runtime file that holds the
# catch point is built with WebAssembly exception handling, which lowers
# setjmp/longjmp to throw and catch (the module links libsetjmp for the
# rest). No other member is built so, and the exnref encoding is LLVM's default.
WASM_SJLJ_avra_runtime.c := -mllvm -wasm-enable-sjlj -mexception-handling
WASM_RUNTIME_SRCS := $(filter-out runtime/avra_cores.c,$(wildcard runtime/*.c))
WASM_RUNTIME_OBJS := $(patsubst runtime/%.c,build/wasm32/%.o,$(WASM_RUNTIME_SRCS))
WASM_RUNTIME_LIB := build/wasm32/libavra_runtime.a

# A WASM OBJECT FOLLOWS ITS SOURCE'S CONTENT AS A HOST OBJECT DOES: it rides
# the same stamp (`build/<stem>.sha`, the headers it names included) and writes
# its own dependency list, so neither a source older than its object nor an
# edited header links a stale member.
build/wasm32/%.o: runtime/%.c build/%.sha
	@mkdir -p build/wasm32
	$(WASM_CC) --target=$(WASM_TARGET) $(if $(WASI_SYSROOT),--sysroot=$(WASI_SYSROOT)) $(WASM_EMULATED) -DAVRA_INSTRUMENTS=$(WASM_INSTRUMENTS) -Iruntime -MMD -MP -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -Oz -Wno-deprecated $(WASM_SJLJ_$(notdir $<)) -c -o $@ $<

# A PACKAGE'S C FOR WASM, from the paths its manifest's `wasm_objects` names.
# A package opts in by naming its wasm objects; one that names none is refused
# by the build, never compiled here.
WASM_PACKAGE_OBJS := $(shell sh tools/manifest_objects.sh --wasm)

build/wasm32/%.o: %.c build/%.sha
	@mkdir -p build/wasm32
	$(WASM_CC) --target=$(WASM_TARGET) $(if $(WASI_SYSROOT),--sysroot=$(WASI_SYSROOT)) $(WASM_EMULATED) -Iruntime -I$(dir $<) -MMD -MP -ffunction-sections -fdata-sections -Oz -Wno-deprecated -c -o $@ $<

-include $(patsubst %.o,%.d,$(WASM_RUNTIME_OBJS) $(WASM_PACKAGE_OBJS))

# THE CORE OBJECT IS THE ARCHIVE'S FIRST MEMBER: the program imports every
# runtime row from `avra:rt`, and a member that names one of them plain
# (`env`) while the row is still undefined is a module mismatch at the link.
# The linker takes members in archive order, so the object that DEFINES the
# rows goes first and nothing meets an undefined one.
$(WASM_RUNTIME_LIB): $(WASM_RUNTIME_OBJS)
	@mkdir -p build/wasm32
	@rm -f $@
